source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Exact source records mapped to established public labels; mapping is recorded for every verse and verified against source KJV annotations. Daniel, Hosea, Joel, Jonah, Micah, and Nahum have chapter-boundary differences.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Preserves occupation, visionary description, both reigns, and earthquake interval without supplying an absolute date.
verses.before: The words of Amos, who was among the shepherds of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
verses.after: These are the words of Amos, who was among the sheep breeders of Tekoa—what he saw concerning Israel during the reigns of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
verses.tsw_comparator: The words of Amos, who was among the shepherds of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.

verses.rationale: Keeps the roar, mournful pasture, and specific mountain; matches Joel's shared formula where clear.
verses.before: He said: The LORD roars from Zion and gives his voice from Jerusalem; the pastures of the shepherds mourn, and the summit of Carmel dries up.
verses.after: He said: “The LORD roars from Zion and raises his voice from Jerusalem. The shepherds’ pastures mourn, and the summit of Carmel dries up.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said: The LORD roars from Zion and gives his voice from Jerusalem; the pastures of the shepherds mourn, and the summit of Carmel dries up.

verses.rationale: Preserves the cumulative number formula and open it; retains the brutal agricultural image.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they threshed Gilead with sledges of iron.
verses.after: This is what the LORD says: “For three rebellions of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn it back: they threshed Gilead with iron threshing sledges.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they threshed Gilead with sledges of iron.

verses.rationale: Keeps dynasty names and the repeated fire/citadel formula.
verses.before: So I will send fire upon the house of Hazael, and it will consume the fortresses of Ben-Hadad.
verses.after: I will send fire into the house of Hazael, and it will consume Ben-hadad’s citadels.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I will send fire upon the house of Hazael, and it will consume the fortresses of Ben-Hadad.

verses.rationale: Retains all place-names and distinguishes inhabitant from ruler rather than silently equating both.
verses.before: I will break the bar of Damascus and cut off the inhabitant from the Valley of Aven and the one who holds the scepter from Beth-Eden. The people of Aram will go into exile to Kir, says the LORD.
verses.after: I will break the gate bar of Damascus, cut off the inhabitant from the Valley of Aven and the scepter-holder from Beth-eden. The people of Aram will go into exile to Kir,” says the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will break the bar of Damascus and cut off the inhabitant from the Valley of Aven and the one who holds the scepter from Beth-Eden. The people of Aram will go into exile to Kir, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves total deportation and transfer destination without importing modern Gaza referents.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Gaza, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they carried into exile a whole population to hand them over to Edom.
verses.after: This is what the LORD says: “For three rebellions of Gaza, and for four, I will not turn it back: they deported an entire community to hand them over to Edom.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Gaza, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they carried into exile a whole population to hand them over to Edom.

verses.rationale: Repeats the judgment form while retaining the city's feminine personification.
verses.before: So I will send fire upon the wall of Gaza, and it will consume her fortresses.
verses.after: I will send fire into Gaza’s wall, and it will consume her citadels.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I will send fire upon the wall of Gaza, and it will consume her fortresses.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three cities, remnant outcome, and adonai/YHWH title convention.
verses.before: I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod and the one who holds the scepter from Ashkelon. I will turn my hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines will perish, says the Lord GOD.
verses.after: I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod and the scepter-holder from Ashkelon. I will turn my hand against Ekron, and the remaining Philistines will perish,” says the Lord GOD.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod and the one who holds the scepter from Ashkelon. I will turn my hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines will perish, says the Lord GOD.

verses.rationale: Preserves deportation and covenant breach as separate charges with kinship language intact.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Tyre, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they handed over a whole population to Edom and did not remember the covenant of brothers.
verses.after: This is what the LORD says: “For three rebellions of Tyre, and for four, I will not turn it back: they handed an entire community over to Edom and did not remember a covenant of brothers.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Tyre, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they handed over a whole population to Edom and did not remember the covenant of brothers.

verses.rationale: Retains the refrain without unnecessary variation.
verses.before: So I will send fire upon the wall of Tyre, and it will consume her fortresses.
verses.after: I will send fire into Tyre’s wall, and it will consume her citadels.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So I will send fire upon the wall of Tyre, and it will consume her fortresses.

verses.rationale: Keeps fraternal violence and sustained personified anger rather than a generic hostility summary.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn it back, because he pursued his brother with the sword and destroyed his compassion. His anger tore continually, and he kept his fury forever.
verses.after: This is what the LORD says: “For three rebellions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn it back: he pursued his brother with a sword and destroyed his compassion. His anger tore on and on; he kept his fury forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn it back, because he pursued his brother with the sword and destroyed his compassion. His anger tore continually, and he kept his fury forever.

verses.rationale: Preserves the two distinct Edomite place-names.
verses.before: So I will send fire upon Teman, and it will consume the fortresses of Bozrah.
verses.after: I will send fire into Teman, and it will consume Bozrah’s citadels.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So I will send fire upon Teman, and it will consume the fortresses of Bozrah.

verses.rationale: Preserves the actual atrocity and explicitly territorial motive.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead in order to enlarge their territory.
verses.after: This is what the LORD says: “For three rebellions of the Ammonites, and for four, I will not turn it back: they ripped open Gilead’s pregnant women to enlarge their territory.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead in order to enlarge their territory.

verses.rationale: Keeps ignite distinct from send and both paired day clauses.
verses.before: So I will kindle fire upon the wall of Rabbah, and it will consume her fortresses with a shout on the day of battle, with a storm on the day of whirlwind.
verses.after: I will set fire to Rabbah’s wall, and it will consume her citadels, amid shouts on the day of battle, amid a whirlwind on the day of storm.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I will kindle fire upon the wall of Rabbah, and it will consume her fortresses with a shout on the day of battle, with a storm on the day of whirlwind.

verses.rationale: Follows pointed their king while noting the possible Milcom name reading.
verses.before: Their king will go into exile, he and his officials together, says the LORD.
verses.after: Their king will go into exile, he and his rulers together,” says the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their king will go into exile, he and his officials together, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the desecration of a foreign king's remains as the stated charge.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Moab, and for four, I will not turn it back, because he burned the bones of the king of Edom to lime.
verses.after: This is what the LORD says: “For three rebellions of Moab, and for four, I will not turn it back: he burned the bones of Edom’s king into lime.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Moab, and for four, I will not turn it back, because he burned the bones of the king of Edom to lime.

verses.rationale: Preserves the proper name and threefold battle soundscape.
verses.before: So I will send fire upon Moab, and it will consume the fortresses of Kerioth. Moab will die amid uproar, with a shout, with the sound of a ram’s horn.
verses.after: I will send fire into Moab, and it will consume Kerioth’s citadels. Moab will die amid uproar, with battle cries and the sound of a ram’s horn.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I will send fire upon Moab, and it will consume the fortresses of Kerioth. Moab will die amid uproar, with a shout, with the sound of a ram’s horn.

verses.rationale: Keeps judge rather than replacing it with king and preserves all rulers.
verses.before: I will cut off the judge from her midst and kill all her officials with him, says the LORD.
verses.after: I will cut off the judge from her midst and kill all her rulers with him,” says the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will cut off the judge from her midst and kill all her officials with him, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains instruction/decrees and lies without silently substituting idols.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Judah, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they rejected the instruction of the LORD and did not keep his statutes. Their lies led them astray, those after which their ancestors walked.
verses.after: This is what the LORD says: “For three rebellions of Judah, and for four, I will not turn it back: they rejected the LORD’s instruction and did not keep his decrees. Their lies led them astray, the lies their ancestors followed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Judah, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they rejected the instruction of the LORD and did not keep his statutes. Their lies led them astray, those after which their ancestors walked.

verses.rationale: Keeps the fire refrain equally applied to Judah.
verses.before: So I will send fire upon Judah, and it will consume the fortresses of Jerusalem.
verses.after: I will send fire into Judah, and it will consume Jerusalem’s citadels.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So I will send fire upon Judah, and it will consume the fortresses of Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Uses innocent in judicial context and retains the concrete low price rather than only saying exploitation.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they sell the righteous for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals—
verses.after: This is what the LORD says: “For three rebellions of Israel, and for four, I will not turn it back: they sell the innocent for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they sell the righteous for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals—

verses.rationale: Follows the difficult pant/crave wording rather than silently emending to trample; preserves sexual abuse context without calling the woman a prostitute.
verses.before: people who pant after the dust of the earth upon the head of the poor and turn aside the way of the humble. A man and his father go in to the same young woman, so that they profane my holy name.
verses.after: They crave even the dust of the ground on the heads of the poor and twist the path of the afflicted. A man and his father go to the same young woman, profaning my holy name.
verses.tsw_comparator: those who pant after the dust of the earth upon the head of the poor and turn aside the way of the humble. A man and his father go in to the same young woman, so that they profane my holy name.

verses.rationale: Connects worship to seized collateral and fines while preserving the physical scene.
verses.before: On garments taken in pledge they stretch themselves beside every altar, and in the house of their God they drink wine from people who have been fined.
verses.after: They stretch out beside every altar on clothes taken as pledges, and in the house of their God they drink wine taken in fines.
verses.tsw_comparator: On garments taken in pledge they stretch themselves beside every altar, and in the house of their God they drink wine from those who have been fined.

verses.rationale: Keeps tree similes and total above/below destruction with divine emphasis.
verses.before: Yet I destroyed the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of cedars and who was strong like the oaks. I destroyed his fruit above and his roots beneath.
verses.after: Yet I destroyed the Amorite before them, tall as cedars and strong as oaks. I destroyed his fruit above and his roots below.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet I destroyed the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of cedars and who was strong like the oaks. I destroyed his fruit above and his roots beneath.

verses.rationale: Preserves forty years and the purpose of the journey.
verses.before: I brought you up from the land of Egypt and led you in the wilderness forty years to possess the land of the Amorite.
verses.after: I brought you up from the land of Egypt and led you through the wilderness for forty years to take possession of the Amorite’s land.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I brought you up from the land of Egypt and led you in the wilderness forty years to possess the land of the Amorite.

verses.rationale: Retains male-specific groups and the Nazirite term rather than generalizing dedication.
verses.before: I raised up some of your sons as prophets and some of your young men as Nazirites. Is this not so, children of Israel? says the LORD.
verses.after: I raised up some of your sons as prophets and some of your young men as Nazirites. Is this not so, people of Israel?” declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: I raised up some of your sons as prophets and some of your young men as Nazirites. Is this not so, children of Israel? says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two direct violations and quoted prohibition.
verses.before: But you made the Nazirites drink wine, and you commanded the prophets, saying, “You will not prophesy.”
verses.after: “But you made the Nazirites drink wine and commanded the prophets, ‘Do not prophesy!’
verses.tsw_comparator: But you made the Nazirites drink wine, and you commanded the prophets, saying, “You shall not prophesy.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the difficult pressure image and notes alternate creaking interpretation.
verses.before: Look, I am pressing down upon you as a cart presses when it is full of sheaves.
verses.after: Now I will press down beneath you as a cart loaded with sheaves presses down.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I am pressing down upon you as a cart presses when it is full of sheaves.

verses.rationale: Keeps the three progressively defeated capacities and repeated escape theme.
verses.before: Flight will perish from the swift, the strong will not strengthen his power, and the warrior will not save his life.
verses.after: The swift will have no escape; the strong will find no strength; the warrior will not save his life.
verses.tsw_comparator: Flight will perish from the swift, the strong will not strengthen his power, and the warrior will not save his life.

verses.rationale: Retains distinct military roles and matches the preceding survival refrain.
verses.before: The one who handles the bow will not stand, the swift of foot will not escape, and the rider of the horse will not save his life.
verses.after: The archer will not stand his ground; the fleet-footed will not escape; the horseman will not save his life.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who handles the bow will not stand, the swift of foot will not escape, and the rider of the horse will not save his life.

verses.rationale: Preserves naked flight and specified day without softening humiliation.
verses.before: Even the stout-hearted among the warriors will flee naked on that day, says the LORD.
verses.after: Even the bravest of warriors will flee naked on that day,” declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even the stout-hearted among the warriors will flee naked on that day, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the sudden first-person divine quotation inside the introductory address.
verses.before: Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, children of Israel, against the whole clan that I brought up from the land of Egypt:
verses.after: Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, people of Israel—against the whole family I brought up from the land of Egypt:
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, children of Israel, against the whole clan that I brought up from the land of Egypt:

verses.rationale: Preserves knowing as relationship and the surprising accountability consequence of election.
verses.before: You only have I known from all the clans of the earth; so I will attend to you for all your guilt.
verses.after: “You alone have I known among all the families of the earth. That is why I will call you to account for all your guilt.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You only have I known from all the clans of the earth; therefore I will attend to you for all your guilt.

verses.rationale: Renders noadu as meeting rather than broad ideological agreement.
verses.before: Do two walk together unless they have met?
verses.after: Do two people walk together unless they have arranged to meet?
verses.tsw_comparator: Do two walk together unless they have met?

verses.rationale: Keeps both causally linked animal questions without explanatory answers.
verses.before: Does a lion roar in the forest when it has no prey? Does a young lion give its voice from its den unless it has captured something?
verses.after: Does a lion roar in the forest when it has no prey? Does a young lion cry from its den unless it has caught something?
verses.tsw_comparator: Does a lion roar in the forest when it has no prey? Does a young lion give its voice from its den unless it has captured something?

verses.rationale: Retains two trap mechanisms as rhetorical cause/effect questions.
verses.before: Does a bird fall into a trap on the ground when there is no snare for it? Does a trap spring up from the ground when it has caught nothing?
verses.after: Does a bird fall into a trap on the ground unless a snare is set for it? Does a trap spring up from the ground without catching anything?
verses.tsw_comparator: Does a bird fall into a trap on the ground when there is no snare for it? Does a trap spring up from the ground when it has caught nothing?

verses.rationale: Preserves the direct divine-agency claim while distinguishing disaster from moral evil.
verses.before: If a ram’s horn is blown in a city, do the people not tremble? If disaster happens in a city, has the LORD not done it?
verses.after: When a ram’s horn sounds in a city, do the people not tremble? When disaster strikes a city, has the LORD not brought it about?
verses.tsw_comparator: If a ram’s horn is blown in a city, do the people not tremble? If disaster happens in a city, has the LORD not done it?

verses.rationale: Keeps the counsel/servants relationship and does not expand it into a modern universal prediction rule.
verses.before: For the Lord GOD does nothing unless he reveals his counsel to his servants the prophets.
verses.after: The Lord GOD does nothing without revealing his counsel to his servants the prophets.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the Lord GOD does nothing unless he reveals his counsel to his servants the prophets.

verses.rationale: Maintains the climactic paired questions and returns to the opening roar.
verses.before: A lion has roared— who will not fear? The Lord GOD has spoken— who can but prophesy?
verses.after: A lion has roared—who will not fear? The Lord GOD has spoken—who will not prophesy?
verses.tsw_comparator: A lion has roared— who will not fear? The Lord GOD has spoken— who can but prophesy?

verses.rationale: Follows pinned Ashdod and summons foreign observers to the city's violence.
verses.before: Proclaim over the fortresses in Ashdod and over the fortresses in the land of Egypt, and say: “Gather yourselves upon the mountains of Samaria and see the great tumults within her and the oppressed in her midst.”
verses.after: Proclaim to the citadels of Ashdod and the citadels in the land of Egypt: “Gather on Samaria’s mountains and see the great turmoil within her and the oppression in her midst.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Proclaim over the fortresses in Ashdod and over the fortresses in the land of Egypt, and say: “Gather yourselves upon the mountains of Samaria and see the great tumults within her and the oppressed in her midst.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the ironic stored wealth of violence and the knowledge diagnosis.
verses.before: They do not know how to do what is right, says the LORD, people who store up violence and devastation in their fortresses.
verses.after: “They do not know how to do right,” declares the LORD, “those who store up violence and plunder in their citadels.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They do not know how to do what is right, says the LORD, those who store up violence and devastation in their fortresses.

verses.rationale: Supplies a verb for the terse encircling enemy and preserves address to personified city.
verses.before: So thus says the Lord GOD: An adversary will surround the land; he will bring down your strength from you, and your fortresses will be plundered.
verses.after: So this is what the Lord GOD says: “An enemy will surround the land, pull down your strength, and plunder your citadels.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: An adversary will surround the land; he will bring down your strength from you, and your fortresses will be plundered.

verses.rationale: Preserves the ironic minimal rescue and difficult Damascus couch phrase rather than inventing secure escape.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: As the shepherd rescues from the lion’s mouth two legs or a piece of an ear, so the children of Israel will be rescued— people who sit in Samaria on the corner of a couch and on a bed in Damascus.
verses.after: This is what the LORD says: “As a shepherd rescues from a lion’s mouth two leg bones or a scrap of ear, so will the people of Israel be rescued— those who sit in Samaria on a corner of a bed and on a Damascus couch.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: As the shepherd rescues from the lion’s mouth two legs or a piece of an ear, so the children of Israel will be rescued— those who sit in Samaria on the corner of a couch and on a bed in Damascus.

verses.rationale: Retains all divine titles and courtroom witness command.
verses.before: Hear and testify against the house of Jacob, says the Lord GOD, the God of Hosts.
verses.after: “Hear and testify against the house of Jacob,” declares the Lord GOD, the God of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear and testify against the house of Jacob, says the Lord GOD, the God of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated accountability verb and concrete altar horns.
verses.before: For on the day I attend to the transgressions of Israel, I will attend to the altars of Bethel. The horns of the altar will be cut off and fall to the ground.
verses.after: “On the day I call Israel to account for his rebellions, I will also call Bethel’s altars to account. The altar’s horns will be cut off and fall to the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: For on the day I attend to the transgressions of Israel, I will attend to the altars of Bethel. The horns of the altar will be cut off and fall to the ground.

verses.rationale: Preserves seasonal luxury residences and ivory without claiming solid-ivory construction.
verses.before: I will strike the winter house together with the summer house. The houses of ivory will perish, and many houses will come to an end, says the LORD.
verses.after: I will strike the winter house together with the summer house. The ivory houses will perish, and many houses will come to an end,” declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will strike the winter house together with the summer house. The houses of ivory will perish, and many houses will come to an end, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Makes the feminine addressees clear while retaining the harsh cattle insult and exploitation.
verses.before: Hear this word, cows of Bashan who are on the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor, who crush the needy, who say to their husbands, “Bring, so that we may drink!”
verses.after: Hear this word, you cows of Bashan on Samaria’s mountain, you women who oppress the poor and crush the needy, who say to your husbands, ‘Bring us something to drink!’
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear this word, cows of Bashan who are on the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor, who crush the needy, who say to their husbands, “Bring, so that we may drink!”

verses.rationale: Preserves oath, captivity, and both hook terms; alternative containers noted.
verses.before: The Lord GOD has sworn by his holiness: Look, days are coming upon you when they will take you away with hooks and the last of you with fishhooks.
verses.after: The Lord GOD has sworn by his holiness: “Days are coming upon you when you will be carried away with hooks, the last of you with fishhooks.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Lord GOD has sworn by his holiness: Look, days are coming upon you when they will take you away with hooks and the last of you with fishhooks.

verses.rationale: Keeps individual female captives and the uncertain destination rather than replacing it with a known location.
verses.before: You will go out through breaches, each woman straight ahead, and you will be cast out toward Harmon, says the LORD.
verses.after: You will go out through breaches in the wall, each woman straight ahead, and you will be flung toward Harmon,” declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will go out through breaches, each woman straight ahead, and you will be cast out toward Harmon, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the sarcasm and literal three days rather than harmonizing to legal three-year tithes.
verses.before: Come to Bethel and transgress; at Gilgal multiply transgression. Bring your sacrifices in the morning, your tithes every three days.
verses.after: “Go to Bethel and rebel! Go to Gilgal and multiply rebellion! Bring your sacrifices every morning and your tithes every three days.
verses.tsw_comparator: Come to Bethel and transgress; at Gilgal multiply transgression. Bring your sacrifices in the morning, your tithes every three days.

verses.rationale: Keeps leavened offering and ostentatious proclamation without smoothing the irony.
verses.before: Burn a thanksgiving offering with leaven and proclaim freewill offerings; make them known, for so you love to do, children of Israel, says the Lord GOD.
verses.after: Burn a thank offering of leavened bread; proclaim freewill offerings—announce them! For that is what you love, people of Israel,” declares the Lord GOD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Burn a thanksgiving offering with leaven and proclaim freewill offerings; make them known, for so you love to do, children of Israel, says the Lord GOD.

verses.rationale: Preserves clean-teeth famine idiom and the exact refrain to recur five times.
verses.before: I also gave you cleanness of teeth in all your cities and lack of bread in all your places; yet you did not return to me, says the LORD.
verses.after: “I gave you clean teeth in all your cities and no bread in any of your settlements. Yet you did not return to me,” declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: I also gave you cleanness of teeth in all your cities and lack of bread in all your places; yet you did not return to me, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the three-month interval and unequal local rainfall rather than general drought alone.
verses.before: I also withheld the rain from you when there were still three months until harvest. I made it rain upon one city and did not make it rain upon another city. One field was rained upon, and the field on which it did not rain dried up.
verses.after: “I also withheld rain from you when harvest was still three months away. I sent rain on one city but not another. One field received rain; the field without rain dried up.
verses.tsw_comparator: I also withheld the rain from you when there were still three months until harvest. I made it rain upon one city and did not make it rain upon another city. One field was rained upon, and the field on which it did not rain dried up.

verses.rationale: Preserves city numbers, exhausted movement, and unchanged refrain.
verses.before: Two or three cities wandered to one city to drink water and were not satisfied; yet you did not return to me, says the LORD.
verses.after: People from two or three cities staggered to one city for water, but they could not drink their fill. Yet you did not return to me,” declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Two or three cities wandered to one city to drink water and were not satisfied; yet you did not return to me, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps all crops and two crop diseases; matches gazam terminology used in Joel.

verses.tsw_comparator: I struck you with blight and mildew. The locust devoured the multitude of your gardens, your vineyards, your fig trees, and your olive trees; yet you did not return to me, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains death, capture, and corpse stench rather than sanitizing the judgment.

verses.rationale: Preserves third-person God inside divine speech and the narrow-rescue image.
verses.before: I overthrew some among you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a burning stick snatched from the fire; yet you did not return to me, says the LORD.
verses.after: “I overthrew some of you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah. You were like a charred stick snatched from a fire. Yet you did not return to me,” declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: I overthrew some among you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a burning stick snatched from the fire; yet you did not return to me, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps this unexplained, as in the source, rather than inventing the threatened action.
verses.before: So thus I will do to you, Israel. Because I will do this to you, prepare to meet your God, Israel!

verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus I will do to you, Israel. Because I will do this to you, prepare to meet your God, Israel!

verses.rationale: Retains creation, disclosure, darkness, and heights; notes ambiguity of whose thought is disclosed.

verses.after: Look: he forms the mountains and creates the wind; he tells human beings what his thought is. He turns dawn to darkness and treads the heights of the earth. The LORD, the God of Armies, is his name.
verses.tsw_comparator: For look, the one who forms the mountains and creates the wind, who declares to humanity what his thought is, who makes dawn into darkness and treads upon the heights of the earth— the LORD, the God of Hosts, is his name.

verses.rationale: Signals the literary form explicitly using qinah's funeral sense.

verses.after: Hear this word I take up over you as a funeral lament, house of Israel:

verses.rationale: Preserves feminine national personification and the unqualified lament before later hope.
verses.before: Fallen, no more to rise, is virgin Israel. She is abandoned upon her ground; there is no one to raise her up.

verses.rationale: Keeps exact thousand/hundred/ten attrition and military movement.

verses.after: For this is what the Lord GOD says: “The city that marches out a thousand will have a hundred left; the one that marches out a hundred will have ten left for the house of Israel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the Lord GOD: The city that goes out with a thousand will have a hundred left, and the one that goes out with a hundred will have ten left for the house of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains the concise imperative linking seeking and life.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD to the house of Israel: Seek me and live.
verses.after: For this is what the LORD says to the house of Israel: “Seek me and live.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD to the house of Israel: Seek me and live.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three pilgrimage sites and Gilgal/exile, Bethel/worthlessness wordplay through a note.

verses.rationale: Keeps the third-person exhortation and Bethel reference rather than substituting Israel.
verses.before: Seek the LORD and live, lest he break out like fire against the house of Joseph and consume it, with no one to extinguish it for Bethel.
verses.after: Seek the LORD and live, or he may sweep through the house of Joseph like fire and consume it, with no one at Bethel to put it out.
verses.tsw_comparator: Seek the LORD and live, lest he break out like fire against the house of Joseph and consume it, with no one to extinguish it for Bethel.

verses.rationale: Retains the bitter plant and discarded righteousness as concrete images.
verses.before: You who turn justice into wormwood and cast righteousness to the ground—
verses.after: You turn justice into wormwood and throw righteousness to the ground!
verses.tsw_comparator: You who turn justice into wormwood and cast righteousness to the ground—

verses.rationale: Keeps both star groups, opposed light transformations, and waters without supplying a mechanism.

verses.tsw_comparator: the one who made the Pleiades and Orion, who turns deep darkness into morning and darkens day into night, who calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out upon the face of the earth— the LORD is his name.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated devastation and suddenness of the rare verb.
verses.before: He flashes destruction upon the strong, so that destruction comes upon the fortress.
verses.after: He flashes devastation upon the strong, and devastation comes upon the fortress.
verses.tsw_comparator: He flashes destruction upon the strong, so that destruction comes upon the fortress.

verses.rationale: Keeps gate as legal setting and the two forms of truthful speech.

verses.rationale: Preserves exploitation, luxury construction, and two frustrated enjoyments.

verses.after: Because you trample the poor and take levies of grain from them, you have built houses of dressed stone, but you will not live in them. You have planted lovely vineyards, but you will not drink their wine.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, because you trample the poor and take a grain tax from him, though you have built houses of cut stone, you will not live in them; though you have planted delightful vineyards, you will not drink their wine.

verses.rationale: Makes the three judicial abuses clear while keeping the gate image.

verses.rationale: States the observation without adding approval of silence.

verses.after: That is why the prudent keep silent at such a time, for it is an evil time.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore the prudent person will be silent in such a time, for it is an evil time.

verses.rationale: Preserves the challenge to claimed divine presence rather than treating it as an unconditional assurance.

verses.after: Seek good, not evil, so that you may live. Then the LORD, the God of Armies, will be with you, as you claim he is.
verses.tsw_comparator: Seek good and not evil, so that you may live; and so the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be with you, as you have said.

verses.rationale: Retains perhaps and the remnant limitation rather than promising automatic pardon.

verses.rationale: Preserves the full title sequence and both ordinary and professional mourners.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine passing-through and reversal of vineyard joy.
verses.before: In all the vineyards there will be wailing, for I will pass through your midst, says the LORD.
verses.after: There will be lamentation in every vineyard, for I will pass through your midst,” says the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: In all the vineyards there will be wailing, for I will pass through your midst, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains two name occurrences and the reversal of desired expectations.
verses.before: Woe to those who desire the day of the LORD! Why is the day of the LORD for you? It is darkness and not light.
verses.after: Woe to you who long for the day of the LORD! What will the day of the LORD mean for you? It will be darkness, not light.
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to those who desire the day of the LORD! Why is the day of the LORD for you? It is darkness and not light.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sequential failed escapes and ordinary gesture at home.

verses.after: It will be like a man fleeing a lion only to meet a bear, or going home, resting his hand on the wall, and being bitten by a snake.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is as when a man flees from a lion and a bear meets him, or he enters the house and leans his hand against the wall and a serpent bites him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated question rather than collapsing it into v18.
verses.before: Is not the day of the LORD darkness and not light, gloom with no brightness in it?
verses.after: Will not the day of the LORD be darkness, not light— gloom without a ray of brightness?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is not the day of the LORD darkness and not light, gloom with no brightness in it?

verses.rationale: Retains two rejection verbs and the smell/savor metaphor.
verses.before: I hate, I reject your festivals, and I will not delight in your solemn assemblies.
verses.after: “I hate, I reject your festivals; I will not savor your solemn assemblies.
verses.tsw_comparator: I hate, I reject your festivals, and I will not delight in your solemn assemblies.

verses.rationale: Keeps the three offering types and successive sensory rejection.

verses.after: Even if you offer me burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them. I will not look upon your fellowship offerings of fattened animals.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even if you offer me your burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them, and the offerings of well-being from your fattened animals I will not look upon.

verses.rationale: Preserves the harsh noise designation and refusal to hear.
verses.before: Remove from me the noise of your songs; I will not listen to the sound of your harps.
verses.after: Take the noise of your songs away from me! I will not listen to the music of your harps.
verses.tsw_comparator: Remove from me the noise of your songs; I will not listen to the sound of your harps.

verses.rationale: Retains familiar clear wording and explains perennial strength through natural English, without novelty for its own sake.

verses.after: Let justice roll like water, and righteousness like a stream that never runs dry.
verses.tsw_comparator: But let justice roll down like waters and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.

verses.rationale: Preserves the difficult historical question without resolving its expected answer in the verse.

verses.after: Did you bring me sacrifices and grain offerings during the forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel?
verses.tsw_comparator: Did you bring me sacrifices and grain offerings in the wilderness forty years, house of Israel?

verses.rationale: Follows pinned names and future exile linkage; notes tense and ancient version alternatives.

verses.after: You will carry Sikkuth your king and Kiyyun your images, the star of your god that you made for yourselves.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall carry Sikkuth your king and Kiyyun your images, the star of your gods that you made for yourselves.

verses.rationale: Retains Damascus rather than harmonizing to a later quotation's Babylon.
verses.before: I will send you into exile beyond Damascus, says the LORD, whose name is the God of Hosts.
verses.after: I will send you into exile beyond Damascus,” says the LORD, whose name is the God of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I will send you into exile beyond Damascus, says the LORD, whose name is the God of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Preserves both capitals and elite self-positioning without limiting the oracle to one city.

verses.after: Woe to those at ease in Zion and those secure on Samaria’s mountain— the renowned men of the foremost nation, to whom the house of Israel comes!

verses.rationale: Keeps the comparison's ambiguous pronouns and all three places.

verses.after: Cross over to Calneh and look; go from there to great Hamath, then down to Gath of the Philistines. Are they better than these kingdoms? Is their territory larger than yours?
verses.tsw_comparator: Cross over to Calneh and see; from there go to Hamath the great; then go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are you better than these kingdoms? Or is their territory greater than your territory?

verses.rationale: Preserves the far/near antithesis and violence's seat/rule image.

verses.after: You push the evil day far away while bringing the reign of violence near.
verses.tsw_comparator: You who put far away the evil day and bring near the seat of violence;

verses.rationale: Keeps physical luxury, posture, and selected meat without adding modern class terminology.

verses.after: You lie on ivory beds and sprawl on couches, eating lambs from the flock and calves from the stall.

verses.after: You improvise to the sound of the harp and invent musical instruments for yourselves like David.
verses.tsw_comparator: who improvise songs to the sound of the harp and, like David, devise instruments for themselves;

verses.rationale: Preserves excess vessels and oil against the ungrieved collective wound.

verses.after: You drink wine from bowls and anoint yourselves with the finest oils, but you do not grieve over Joseph’s ruin.
verses.tsw_comparator: who drink wine from bowls and anoint themselves with the finest oils, but are not grieved over the ruin of Joseph.

verses.rationale: Keeps the first-in-status to first-in-exile reversal and repeats sprawling.

verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore now they will go into exile at the head of the exiles, and the revelry of those who sprawl will pass away.

verses.rationale: Preserves oath and both divine-name occurrences with titles intact.

verses.after: The Lord GOD has sworn by himself, declares the LORD, the God of Armies: “I detest Jacob’s pride and hate his citadels. I will hand over the city and everything in it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The Lord GOD has sworn by himself, says the LORD, the God of Hosts: I abhor the pride of Jacob and hate his fortresses, and I will hand over the city and all that fills it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the precise ten and total survival reversal.

verses.after: If ten men remain in one house, they too will die.

For the name of the LORD must not be mentioned.”

verses.rationale: Keeps both house sizes and distinct destruction images.

verses.rationale: Follows pinned oxen rather than redividing into sea; retains absurdity and poisoned fruit.

verses.rationale: Retains place-names whose meanings nothing/horns carry the boast's irony; explains in note.

verses.rationale: Keeps unnamed invader and both territorial endpoints.

verses.rationale: Preserves timing relative to royal harvest without inventing a tax percentage.

verses.rationale: Keeps the prophet's intercession and weakness argument rather than an innocence claim.

verses.rationale: Keeps Isaac's uncommon spelling/name and dynasty rather than king alone.

verses.rationale: Makes the bread-as-livelihood idiom readable while retaining seer as distinct term.

verses.after: Amaziah told Amos, “Seer, go! Flee to the land of Judah. Earn your bread there, and prophesy there.

verses.rationale: Preserves the political ownership claim and two designations.
verses.before: But at Bethel you will no longer prophesy, for it is the king’s sanctuary and it is a royal house.”

verses.rationale: Chooses past tense in context but notes Hebrew verbless present alternative and guild sense of son.

verses.after: Amos answered Amaziah, “I was no prophet, nor a prophet’s son. I was a herdsman and a tender of sycamore figs.

verses.rationale: Retains both divine names and direct commissioning against professional livelihood framing.

verses.after: But the LORD took me from following the flock, and the LORD told me, ‘Go, prophesy to my people Israel.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the dripping/pouring speech image without making it literal rain.

verses.after: Now hear the word of the LORD. You say, ‘Do not prophesy against Israel; do not pour out words against the house of Isaac.’

verses.rationale: Retains the full family catastrophe and ritual uncleanness without attributing voluntary choice to the wife.

verses.rationale: Keeps the visual object that grounds the coming wordplay.
verses.before: Thus the Lord GOD showed me: Look, a basket of summer fruit.
verses.after: This is what the Lord GOD showed me: a basket of summer fruit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus the Lord GOD showed me: Look, a basket of summer fruit.

verses.rationale: Retains summer fruit/end wordplay in its actual nouns, explained in note, and repeats the earlier no-passing declaration.
verses.before: He said, “What do you see, Amos?” I said, “A basket of summer fruit.” Then the LORD said to me: “The end has come upon my people Israel. I will no longer pass by him.
verses.after: He asked, “What do you see, Amos?” I answered, “A basket of summer fruit.” Then the LORD said to me, “The end has come for my people Israel. I will no longer pass them by.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “What do you see, Amos?” And I said, “A basket of summer fruit.” Then the LORD said to me: “The end has come upon my people Israel. I will no longer pass by him.

verses.rationale: Preserves abrupt corpse fragments and hush; temple/palace alternative noted.
verses.before: The songs of the palace will become wailings on that day,” says the Lord GOD. “Many will be the corpses; in every place they will throw them down. Silence!”
verses.after: The temple songs will turn to wailing on that day,” declares the Lord GOD. “So many bodies, thrown everywhere! Hush!”
verses.tsw_comparator: The songs of the palace will become wailings on that day,” says the Lord GOD. “Many will be the corpses; in every place they will throw them down. Silence!”

verses.rationale: Keeps the predatory panting root and explicit destructive purpose.
verses.before: Hear this, you who trample the needy and bring the poor of the land to an end,
verses.after: Hear this, you who pant after the needy to make the poor of the land cease to exist,
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear this, you who trample the needy and bring the poor of the land to an end,

verses.rationale: Preserves holy-day impatience and each fraudulent measurement mechanism.

verses.rationale: Repeats the sandals motif and keeps sale of inferior remnants concrete.

verses.rationale: Preserves the ambiguous oath object instead of replacing pride with a chosen referent.
verses.before: The LORD has sworn by the Pride of Jacob: “Surely I will never forget any of their deeds.
verses.after: The LORD has sworn by the pride of Jacob: “I will never forget any of their deeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has sworn by the Pride of Jacob: “Surely I will never forget any of their deeds.

verses.rationale: Follows read sink and preserves river motion as earthquake imagery.
verses.before: Will not the land tremble because of this, and everyone who lives in it mourn? All of it will rise like the Nile, be tossed about, and sink again like the Nile of Egypt.
verses.after: Will not the land shake for this, and everyone living in it mourn? The whole land will rise like the Nile, toss and sink like Egypt’s Nile.
verses.tsw_comparator: Will not the land tremble because of this, and everyone who lives in it mourn? All of it will rise like the Nile, be tossed about, and sink again like the Nile of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Keeps noon and daylight without identifying a historical eclipse.
verses.before: “And it will be on that day,” says the Lord GOD, “I will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight.
verses.after: On that day,” declares the Lord GOD, “I will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And it will be on that day,” says the Lord GOD, “I will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight.

verses.rationale: Preserves all mourning practices and only-child comparison.
verses.before: I will turn your festivals into mourning and all your songs into lamentation. I will bring sackcloth upon every waist and baldness upon every head. I will make it like mourning for an only child, and its end like a bitter day.
verses.after: I will turn your festivals into mourning and all your songs into funeral laments. I will put sackcloth on every waist and baldness on every head. I will make it like mourning for an only child, and its end like a bitter day.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will turn your festivals into mourning and all your songs into lamentation. I will bring sackcloth upon every waist and baldness upon every head. I will make it like mourning for an only child, and its end like a bitter day.

verses.rationale: Retains the shift from physical scarcity to lack of hearing, not lack of written books.
verses.before: “Look, days are coming,” says the Lord GOD, “when I will send a famine upon the land— not a famine for bread and not a thirst for water, but for hearing the words of the LORD.
verses.after: Days are coming,” declares the Lord GOD, “when I will send a famine through the land— not hunger for bread or thirst for water, but for hearing the words of the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Look, days are coming,” says the Lord GOD, “when I will send a famine upon the land— not a famine for bread and not a thirst for water, but for hearing the words of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the unusual directional pair rather than filling all compass points.
verses.before: They will wander from sea to sea and from north to east; they will roam about seeking the word of the LORD, but they will not find it.
verses.after: They will stagger from sea to sea, from north to east. They will roam in search of the word of the LORD but will not find it.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will wander from sea to sea and from north to east; they will roam about seeking the word of the LORD, but they will not find it.

verses.rationale: Preserves both groups and physical fainting.
verses.before: On that day the beautiful young women and the young men will faint from thirst.
verses.after: On that day beautiful young women and young men will faint from thirst.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day the beautiful young women and the young men will faint from thirst.

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult Guilt and way oath objects, with deity-name alternatives in note.
verses.before: People who swear by the guilt of Samaria and say, “As your god lives, O Dan,” and, “As the way of Beersheba lives,” they will fall and never rise again.
verses.after: Those who swear by Samaria’s Guilt, who say, ‘As your god lives, Dan!’ and ‘As the way of Beer-sheba lives!’— they will fall and never rise again.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who swear by the guilt of Samaria and say, “As your god lives, O Dan,” and, “As the way of Beersheba lives,” they will fall and never rise again.

verses.rationale: Keeps the violent sanctuary collapse and both repeated no-escape assertions.
verses.before: I saw the Lord standing beside the altar, and he said: “Strike the capitals so that the thresholds shake, and break them upon the heads of all of them. The last of them I will kill with the sword. No fugitive among them will escape, and no survivor among them will get away.
verses.after: I saw the Lord standing beside the altar. He said: “Strike the capital so the thresholds shake; bring them down on everyone’s heads. Those who remain I will kill with the sword. No fugitive will get away; no escapee will survive.
verses.tsw_comparator: I saw the Lord standing beside the altar, and he said: “Strike the capitals so that the thresholds shake, and break them upon the heads of all of them. The last of them I will kill with the sword. No fugitive among them will escape, and no survivor among them will get away.

verses.rationale: Preserves cosmological extremes and repeated from there.
verses.before: Though they dig into Sheol, from there my hand will take them. Though they climb up to the heavens, from there I will bring them down.
verses.after: Even if they dig into Sheol, my hand will take them from there. Even if they climb to heaven, I will bring them down from there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Though they dig into Sheol, from there my hand will take them. Though they climb up to the heavens, from there I will bring them down.

verses.rationale: Keeps mountain/deep-sea contrast and unnamed serpent without modern zoological identification.
verses.before: Though they hide themselves on the summit of Carmel, from there I will search them out and take them. Though they hide from my eyes at the bottom of the sea, from there I will command the serpent, and it will bite them.
verses.after: Even if they hide on Carmel’s summit, I will search them out and take them from there. Even if they conceal themselves from my eyes on the seabed, I will command the serpent there to bite them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Though they hide themselves on the summit of Carmel, from there I will search them out and take them. Though they hide from my eyes at the bottom of the sea, from there I will command the serpent, and it will bite them.

verses.rationale: Preserves captivity as no refuge and the reversal of divine watchfulness.
verses.before: Though they go into captivity before their enemies, from there I will command the sword, and it will kill them. I will set my eyes upon them for harm and not for good.”
verses.after: Even if they go into captivity before their enemies, I will command the sword there to kill them. I will set my eyes upon them for harm, not for good.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Though they go into captivity before their enemies, from there I will command the sword, and it will kill them. I will set my eyes upon them for harm and not for good.”

verses.rationale: Keeps melt and mourning with the repeated Nile motion.
verses.before: The Lord GOD of Hosts— the one who touches the earth and it melts, and everyone who live in it mourn; all of it rises like the Nile and sinks again like the Nile of Egypt;
verses.after: The Lord GOD of Armies touches the earth, and it melts; everyone living in it mourns. The whole earth rises like the Nile and sinks like Egypt’s Nile.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Lord GOD of Hosts— the one who touches the earth and it melts, and all who live in it mourn; all of it rises like the Nile and sinks again like the Nile of Egypt;

verses.rationale: Retains ancient architectural cosmology and repeats the water formula.
verses.before: the one who builds his upper chambers in the heavens and establishes his vault upon the earth; who calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out upon the face of the earth— the LORD is his name.
verses.after: He builds his upper chambers in the heavens and founds his vault upon the earth. He calls for the sea’s waters and pours them over the earth’s surface. The LORD is his name.
verses.tsw_comparator: the one who builds his upper chambers in the heavens and establishes his vault upon the earth; who calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out upon the face of the earth— the LORD is his name.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three migrations and the Cushite comparison without reducing it to a modern racial argument.
verses.before: “Are you not like the children of Cush to me, children of Israel?” says the LORD. “Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor, and Aram from Kir?
verses.after: “Are you not like the Cushites to me, people of Israel?” declares the LORD. “Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt, the Philistines from Caphtor, and Aram from Kir?
verses.tsw_comparator: “Are you not like the children of Cush to me, children of Israel?” says the LORD. “Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor, and Aram from Kir?

verses.rationale: Preserves distinction between kingdom destroyed and house not totally destroyed.
verses.before: Look, the eyes of the Lord GOD are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from the face of the ground— except that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob,” says the LORD.
verses.after: Look, the eyes of the Lord GOD are on the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from the face of the ground. Yet I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob,” declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, the eyes of the Lord GOD are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from the face of the ground— except that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Follows pebble for tseror rather than substituting grain and flags the image's interpretive implications.

verses.after: “I will give the command and shake the house of Israel among all the nations as something is shaken in a sieve, without a pebble falling to the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: “For look, I am commanding, and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations as one shakes with a sieve, yet not a pebble will fall to the ground.

verses.rationale: Keeps the specified boast and limits all to sinners among the people.

verses.after: All the sinners among my people will die by the sword— those who say, ‘Disaster will never approach or overtake us.’

verses.rationale: Retains shelter rather than silently palace and the three restorative actions.

verses.rationale: Keeps overlapping agricultural seasons and literal melting hills rather than adding an explanation into poetry.

verses.rationale: Preserves the reversal of denied enjoyment in5:11 through the paired actions.

verses.after: I will restore the fortunes of my people Israel. They will rebuild devastated cities and live in them, plant vineyards and drink their wine, make gardens and eat their fruit.

verses.after: I will plant them in their own ground, and they will never again be uprooted from the ground I have given them,” says the LORD your God.
